summary: Falkon Systems: embedding index reconciliation mismatch & audit-log delivery gap during high ingest (billing exposure)
description:
Issue summary:
During a peak ingest window on 2026-03-10 08:45–09:20 PST, Falkon Systems reported that semantic search results returned incorrect document ids for a subset of recently ingested vectors. Simultaneously, audit logs for ingestion latency and billing counters were missing for a 22-minute interval which prevented Falkon from reconciling billed usage.

Impact:
- Customer-facing search returned stale or mismatched results for ~3.2% of queries routed to the dense-index-service in us-west-2.
- Falkon reported a billing delta (observed vs expected) of ~12% for the ingestion window due to missing audit log events.
- Customer escalated to enterprise support; legal/finance looped in for potential credits.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer-managed VPC peering) in us-west-2 using embedding-encoder-v2 -> dense-index-service (quantized).
- Autoscale pool scaled up at 08:40 but indexer pod restarts were observed between 08:46 and 08:53.

Steps to reproduce (investigation checklist rather than deterministic repro):
1) Ingest high-throughput batch (approx 18k vectors/min) with mixed small and large payloads.
2) Observe indexer task restarts in the dense-index kube pool.
3) Run sample search for recently ingested document ids and compare to precomputed vector->id map.
4) Check audit-log stream for missing log sequence numbers in the 08:45–09:07 window.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Observability trace: https://observability.redwood.internal/traces/2026-03-10/idx-mismatch-08-47
- Grafana panel: embeddings-indexer pod restarts: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/embeddings/indexer-pod-restarts?from=2026-03-10T08:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T09:30:00Z
- Billing delta dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/billing/deltas/falkon/2026-03-10

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Switched Falkon to a pinned read-route that bypasses the in-flight indexer shard (read-only replication) while we replayed the missing events into the index.
- Issued temporary billing credit to cover immediately visible delta pending reconciliation.

Customer impact and communication:
- Customer was updated on-call and received an interim timeline within 30 minutes. Finance requested formal reconciliation and credits; CS opened this ticket to coordinate post-incident follow-up and evidence delivery.
comments: 2026-03-10T09:05Z - Lydia Park (Customer Success): Customer on the line; reporting returned results pointing to wrong doc ids. They can reproduce against queries hitting us-west. Asked for immediate mitigation and credit hold. Escalating to SRE.

2026-03-10T09:12Z - Priya Nair (SRE): Observed 3 indexer pod restarts starting 08:46. Restarted due to OOM eviction on node gpu-12. Raising hypothesis: burst ingest + large batch led to memory pressure on indexer causing partial write batches to be lost before durable ack to audit log stream.

2026-03-10T09:30Z - Evan Chen (Engineer, Index Service): Found gaps in RSM (replicated state machine) commit log for shard-7 between 08:46:23 and 08:58:41. Some commit entries were retained in local ephemeral storage but not flushed to the audit-log producer before the process restart.

2026-03-10T10:10Z - Raul Mendez (Falkon DevOps): Confirmed behavior from our side: ~11% of recent ingest batch ids not present when we ran verification against our sidecar map. Appreciate the temp read-route fix. Need formal reconciliation file and proof of replay before we close billing request.

2026-03-11T14:22Z - Marco Ortega (Assignee): Replay completed and verified. Attached reconciliation CSV to customer Slack and Confluence. Initiated billing adjustment flow. Planning a postmortem and longer-term fix (persistent commit flush before ack).

2026-03-12T16:00Z - Aisha Kumari (Support): Customer accepted reconciliation and billing credit. Customer asked for a timeline for persistent fix and a test plan for future peak ingest scenarios. Added to post-incident action items.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 08:40: autoscaler increased indexer pool to handle surge; several indexer pods scheduled onto new GPU node types.
- 08:46: node gpu-12 experienced transient memory pressure; kernel OOM killed indexer process leading to abrupt restart.
- 08:46–08:59: RSM commit log had unflushed entries that were not propagated to the audit-log Kafka topic due to in-memory batching.
- 08:59–09:10: indexer recovered, but some vector->id mappings were written to ephemeral local store only; replication missed the durable ack.
Root cause hypothesis:
- Combination of aggressive in-memory batching in the dense-index-service and a recent change that increased batch size for latency optimization caused larger transient memory usage. When a pod was OOM-killed, in-memory batch in producer was lost before flush to audit log, creating both search inconsistency and missing billing events.
Contributing factors:
- Autoscaler packed pods onto a smaller set of nodes during the burst (bin-packing behavior).
- No enforced pre-ack flush semantics for commit batches on indexer restart.
Evidence:
- Commit log gaps in index shard-7 trace.
- Missing sequence ranges in audit-log topic for 08:46–09:07.
- Pod OOM event records on node gpu-12.
- Replayed entries successfully restored search parity and reduced billing delta to <0.2%.
resolution_notes:
Immediate remediation:
1) Executed controlled replay of missing commit ranges into indexer from durable write-ahead log stored in object storage.
2) Temporarily pinned Falkon read-route to read-only replica while replay completed.
3) Issued pro-rated billing credit covering the measured delta; finance notified and reconciliation file delivered.
Permanent fixes applied (short-term):
- Rolled out indexer v2.1.3 which reduces in-memory batch size under memory pressure and forces flush on SIGTERM.
- Autoscaler safety adjustment to avoid bin-packing sensitive pods onto a single node by setting podAntiAffinity hints in dense-index-service deploy.
- Added alert rule for audit-log sequence gaps and a check for commit-flush duration > 2s.
Follow-up verification:
- Post-deploy canary with synthetic high-throughput ingest (20k vectors/min) passed for 3 consecutive 30-minute windows with no commit gaps.
Customer communication:
- Shared reconciliation CSV, replay proof, and audit-log segment references. Finance accepted credit; customer closed the escalation after verification.

Adjust autoscaler bin-packing policy for indexer class pods (owner: Priya Nair) - due 2026-03-18
Run a cross-team runbook review session with SRE, Indexing, and Billing to validate audit-log handoff semantics (owner: Marco Ortega) - due 2026-03-25
Provide Falkon with a monthly report for two months showing post-fix ingest parity and billing reconciliations (owner: Lydia Park) - deliver by 2026-04-10
Add an observability dashboard to surface audit-log sequence continuity per-customer and per-shard (owner: Observability Team) - due 2026-03-22
